text:
maya: Heads up — bringing up reranker rv2a in staging. Quick summary: overall NDCG@10 +1.3% but MRR@10 on short queries (len<=6) is down -3.1%. Putting result table below and asking for quick triage.

sean: Short queries only? any breakdown by answer density or top1 EM?

maya: Yup, split by query_len and answer_density. Quick paste from staging run: 
```
metric      overall   short_q (<=6)   long_q (>6)
NDCG@10     +1.3%     +2.0%            +0.8%
MRR@10      -0.7%     -3.1%            +0.9%
Top1_EM     -1.1%     -4.8%            +0.2%
Top3_EM     +0.6%     +0.9%            +0.4%
```
Notable: we changed tokenizer normalization to NFKC + lowercasing, and enabled ctx_wrap candidate context for rv2a. Both were intentional to help long passages.

li: Did we also change candidate formatting/dedupe? I remember a recent PR that strips punctuation before dedupe. That could reduce exact-match signals for short queries.

maya: Yes — candidate_normalize=strip_punc in the new pipeline. Hypothesis: ctx_wrap + lowercasing + strip punctuation reduce exact-match signals for short queries -> drop in MRR and Top1. NDCG can increase if model spreads probability across more relevant items.

rachel: Can you repro by toggling ctx_wrap off in staging and keeping the new model? Also try fp16 vs int8 PTQ — might be an interaction.

sean: I did a quick isolate: switching to int8 PTQ increases short-query MRR drop by ~0.5pp vs fp16 but doesn't explain the whole -3.1pp. So quantization aggravates but probably not primary cause.

maya: Repro command I'm using: 
```
./eval_rerank.sh --model rv2a --dataset holdout_v3 \
  --ctx_wrap {true,false} --tok_norm {nfkc,none} --quant {fp16,int8}
```
Staging run queued.

deploy-bot: Job 61234 queued by maya. ETA ~25m.

li: Also check ordering: earlier pipeline preserved punctuation and candidate slots; now with strip_punc we may be merging candidates differently which affects top-1.

rachel: Agreed. Suggest two quick experiments: (A) ctx_wrap=false with new model (B) keep ctx_wrap but revert tokenizer normalization and punctuation strip. Compare MRR/top1 for short queries. If either recovers MRR -> formatting/priming.

maya: On it. If it's formatting, that's an easier configuration fix than changing the model. If it's quantization+formatting interaction we may need to tweak PTQ calibration or add a short-query priming wrapper.

sean: Also add exact-match rate and top1 probability mass as metrics — MRR is sensitive to top-1. If top1 drops and top3 rises, that's consistent with NDCG up / MRR down pattern.

maya: Current numbers: short_q top1_prob delta ~ -4.3pp, top3_prob +1.2pp. So top-1 is taking the hit.

rachel: :thumbsup: If experiments show formatting is the root cause we can implement a short-query tokenization exception: use legacy tokenizer for queries <=6 tokens. Low-risk and reversible.

li: Also flag to infra/ops: if staging shows regression hold the Dedicated rollout for rv2a until we verify config toggles.

maya: Will do. I queued the staging comparisons. Will post results here.

deploy-bot: Job 61234 completed. Results: staging run with ctx_wrap=false, tok_norm=none, quant=fp16 finished.

maya: Quick update: ctx_wrap=false + tok_norm=none + fp16 -> short_q MRR recovered ~+2.9% (now only -0.2% vs baseline). So formatting+ctx_wrap explains majority. Next test: same but quant=int8.

sean: So fp16 recovery implies formatting/ctx_wrap is dominant, int8 still a smaller contributor. Good to know.

rachel: Let's run a 10% prod A/B: route short queries to config {ctx_wrap=false, legacy_tok} for rv2a and collect online MRR/top1 for 4 hours. If clean, ship config change globally. I'll draft rollout docs.

maya: Filed rollout: https://go/rollout/rv2a-shortquery-config and scheduled 10% for 4h. Will attach result chart.

li: Thanks — nice triage. If A/B holds we'll keep int8 recipe but add per-layer calibration tweak for short-query sensitive slices.

maya: Will follow up with final numbers. Thanks all.
